record.title: Irish Sky Garden — Crater Interior (3D Model)
record.material: Earth and stone; central reclining plinth of Kilkenny granite
record.museum: Liss Ard Estate, Skibbereen, County Cork, Ireland
record.note: Turrell’s grass-lined crater frames the open sky for a reclining viewer. This third-party 3D model represents the crater interior, including the central plinth and stair opening. It is a partial spatial representation: the outer landscape and entrance passage are absent, and the terrain ends at an irregular open boundary. It does not reproduce the changing sky or the experience of being inside the work. The publisher does not document the capture method.
record.scan_source: Third-party 3D model of the crater interior. Capture method undocumented by the publisher; the source was obtained through Sketchfab’s signed-in download control. Geometry optimized and textures resized for browser display; no geometry added to close or extend the source.
record.attribution: Irish Sky Garden — Crater Interior (3D Model). Artwork: James Turrell. 3D model: dkemp; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: Geometry optimized and textures resized for browser display; no geometry added to close or extend the source.

license_evidence.title: James Turrell - Irish Sky Garden
license_evidence.source_acquisition: Normal signed-in Sketchfab download, maximum 8k GLB; downloaded 2026-09-28. Original FBX zip preserved separately.
license_evidence.integrity_basis: SHA256 of downloaded bytes recorded at acquisition and checked after copying; no independent publisher checksum supplied.
license_evidence.license_review: CC grant checked on the live model record and the signed-in download dialog; source bytes hashed at download and rechecked after copying. Current model retains the same qualifying license.

visual_review.note: All four oblique views and independent overhead/bottom views inspected. Central plinth, stair opening and grass bowl agree with estate aerial photographs. Accepted specifically as a partial crater-interior representation; irregular open terrain boundary, absent exterior and entrance passage are disclosed. No metric AR binding. Y-up orientation is correct.

dimensions_review.note: The estate publishes an elliptical crater extent of 50 × 25 m and a 32 m entrance passage. Those dimensions do not establish the extent of this partial model, whose boundary differs; no metric scale is assigned. The chosen starting display size is not a measurement of the artwork. Model coordinates are not calibrated to these measurements.
dimensions_review.spatialNote: Physical size is not documented. Display size is adjustable.

record.note: Interlocking blocks of Aji granite make solid mass and empty space seem to trade places. Rough and polished faces retain the marks of the stone. This photogrammetry scan preserves the lighting present during capture.

record.attribution: Illusion of the Fifth Stone. Artwork: Isamu Noguchi. 3D model: John Briscella; CC BY 4.0. record.title: Woman
record.museum: The Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum, New York
record.note: A vertical basalt form balances dark polished cuts against the stone’s rough outer surface. The irregular mass suggests a standing body without describing one literally. The scan includes the granite base and preserves lighting from the museum capture. The base has a slightly irregular edge where the scan meets the floor.
record.scan_source: Photogrammetry scan; exact open-licensed Objaverse archive version. Surrounding floor trimmed along its measured sloping plane; disconnected peripheral floor patches removed; geometry and textures optimized for browser display. Sculpture and granite base retained.
record.attribution: Woman. Artwork: Isamu Noguchi. 3D model: John Briscella; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: Surrounding floor trimmed along its measured sloping plane; disconnected peripheral floor patches removed; geometry and textures optimized for browser display. Sculpture and granite base retained.

record.title: Fallen Star (Digital Reconstruction)
record.material: Steel framing, concrete and mixed materials; architectural installation
record.museum: Stuart Collection, University of California San Diego, United States
record.note: Suh places a tilted cottage above Jacobs Hall, making a familiar home feel dislocated. This 2016 digital reconstruction by Shaira Tuazon is a simplified exterior study of the cottage and rooftop garden. It omits the furnished interior and the full supporting tower; proportions, planting and architectural details are approximate.
record.scan_author: Shaira Tuazon, DML Consultant; published by CHEI – UC San Diego
record.scan_source: Independent digital reconstruction; exact CC BY 4.0 Objaverse archive version. Geometry and textures optimized for browser display. Not a photogrammetry scan.
record.attribution: Fallen Star (Digital Reconstruction). Artwork: Do Ho Suh. 3D reconstruction: Shaira Tuazon, DML Consultant; published by CHEI – UC San Diego; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: geometry and textures optimized for browser display.

license_evidence.title: Fallen Star
license_evidence.description:
Fallen Star is an art installation by Korean artist Do Ho Suh on the grounds of the University of California, San Diego. It is a house perched at an angle off the edge of the main Jacobs School of Engineering building. (wiki)

Model created by Shaira Tuazon, DML Consultant
license_evidence.scan_author: Shaira Tuazon, DML Consultant; published by CHEI – UC San Diego

visual_review.note: The exterior house, roof, chimney, windows, door, simplified garden/path and rectangular support are coherent across four views. The furnished interior and full Jacobs Hall tower are intentionally not represented, and the model is not a full immersive simulation.

record.title: Indução do Amarelo (Digital Reconstruction)
record.museum: Museu Internacional de Escultura Contemporânea, Santo Tirso, Portugal
record.note: Three inclined panels carry black and blue-gray lines on white; their interaction is intended to induce the perception of yellow. This independent 2017 SketchUp reconstruction uses a photographic texture on simplified panels. Its ground block and human scale figure are contextual modeling elements. It does not reproduce or guarantee the original optical experience.
record.scan_source: Independent digital reconstruction; exact CC BY 4.0 Objaverse archive version. Geometry and textures optimized for browser display. Not a photogrammetry scan.
record.attribution: Indução do Amarelo (Digital Reconstruction). Artwork: Carlos Cruz-Diez. 3D reconstruction: PedroTeixeira; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: geometry and textures optimized for browser display.

exhibition_placements.text: Noguchi sets polished cuts against the rough skin of basalt. Moving around the stone changes the balance between reflective planes, dark openings and untouched surfaces.

excluded_or_held.title: Schurenbachhalde (implemented design)
excluded_or_held.description:
The Schurenbach spoil tip was used to store excavated material of the Zollverein mine until its closure in 1986 and of other coal mines until the mid-1990s. The pile was then renaturalised and converted into a landscape monument where the sculpture Bramme by the American artist Richard Serra, erected in 1998, remains as a landmark. The Schurenbach pile is part of the Route of Industrial Heritage and is due to become part of the 2027 International Garden Exhibition.

The airborne lidar is provided as open access from the Spatial Data portal of North Rhine-Westphalia and was cleaned, colored, segmented, downsampled, as a point cloud model with cloud compare.
